- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to revert; apply mean reversion correction by reducing forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model underreacts to short-term volatility; increase forecast sensitivity to recent price moves.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for negative sentiment periods.  
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting upward; apply 2–3 day lag correction to forecast rise.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 10-day average is > 10% above 30d average, reduce forecast by 3–5% to align with historical mean reversion.
